headline: Models unifying sequences, structures, and language for biomolecular representation
label: Multimodal Molecular Representation Learning
summary: BioMatrix, CellOS, and related 2026 preprints extend multimodal biological representations across sequences, structures, text, and single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning reusable representations of molecules, proteins, RNA, and cells by coupling heterogeneous views such as sequences, structures, knowledge graphs, and natural language. BioMatrix places SMILES/SELFIES, molecular and protein structures, and natural language in one discrete token space within a decoder-only model. CellTosg2Sequence encodes a 62,507-node biomedical knowledge graph as virtual tokens for a single-cell LLM, trained with KG-anchored SFT and GRPO. CellOS aligns expression and perception views through LLM-JEPA across 390.5M transcriptomes. ZHMolTopoRPI and BioGraphX fuse sequence-derived graph or topological features with ESM2 or ESM-2 embeddings for RNA-protein interaction and subcellular localization prediction. Other items, including the SP-Mind agent and SPEAK spatial prompting, apply LLMs to imaging and transcriptomic analysis rather than representation learning per se. The newer element is the explicit incorporation of structured knowledge and heterogeneous modalities into a shared input space.
